event: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker
summary: All 14 bouts (28 fighters) stand, and everyone made weight at Friday's official weigh-ins (Nov 6): UFC.com's live results (cross-checked against Cageside Press and MMA Weekly via Yahoo) list every fighter at or under the 1 lb non-title allowance, with no misses, catchweights or fines. Several were right on the allowance: Jandiroba 116, Elekana 206, Cachoeira and Milosevic 136, Degli and Fernandes 126, Magomedov 146, Kondratavicius 186, Ko, Turman and Souza 171. Main event: Cortes-Acosta 262, Walker 239. Kondratavicius and Turman were the last two weights posted. The only fight-week change: Lucas Brennan (torn ACL) is out, and Fury FC featherweight champion Carlos Calderon replaced him against Austin Bashi on four days' notice (Nov 4), making his UFC debut; he weighed 145.5. Before fight week, Sean Brady (staph infection in his left knee) withdrew from the Bonfim vs. Brady main event, Bonfim was removed from the card, and Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker was elevated to a five-round headliner on about a week's notice (Oct 29). Walker wrote that he 'started the camp today' on about Oct 30-31. Cortes-Acosta has a new coach and new training partners. Andre Petroski arrived from the Oct 31 card after his Bekoev bout was scrapped. Jonny Parsons (three-year layoff) and Wellington Turman (off since Dec 2023) return from long layoffs.

Signed on four days' notice to replace Lucas Brennan (torn ACL) against Austin Bashi; UFC debut. He is 11-4 (1 NC) on a three-fight win streak and defended his Fury FC featherweight title over five rounds against Lorram Esteves in October.
Was originally scheduled to defend his Fury FC title in the Fury FC 127 main event on Jan 15; submitted by Alberto Montes on the 2024 Contender Series.
Opponent changed from Lucas Brennan (torn ACL) to Carlos Calderon. This is the last fight on Bashi's current UFC contract.
DraftKings odds via ClutchPoints: Bashi -535, Calderon +400.
Wrote on Instagram after the main-event booking that he 'started the camp today'; the bout is five rounds, about a week out.
At media day called it 'a really quick turnaround' after getting the offer about a week out: 'I wanted to work my way up slowly, but my plans are not God's plans.'

Has a new coach and new training partners, alongside longtime partner Tyrell Fortune; says he is '100% confident'. Took the fight on a little more than a week's notice after back-to-back decision losses (Volkov, Blaydes). No injuries mentioned.
At media day said Walker 'doesn't have a chin' and that he will go after him.
Wants the next strawweight title shot against Mackenzie Dern with a win; says she always looks to finish. No injury, camp or weight-cut issues mentioned.
Wants a title rematch with Mackenzie Dern and believes she needs a finish to send 'a message'; wants to be 'more forceful' in a rematch. No injury, camp or weight-cut issues mentioned.

Attributes his three-year layoff (last fought July 2023) to bad training habits and lingering injuries he thinks smarter strength and conditioning would have prevented; now prioritises strength before volume.
Returns from a layoff dating to Dec 2, 2023, his longest; on a three-fight losing streak, no win since February 2022.
On a three-fight losing streak, no win since February 2025.
